name: FRED MORTGAGE30US (Freddie Mac Primary Mortgage Market Survey, 30-yr fixed rate, via FRED API)
gap: backend/app/scoring/investment.py:21 hardcodes `interest_rate: float = 0.065` with no data behind it -- every IRR/cash-flow projection in the investment model uses a static guess instead of a live financing assumption.
coverage: National, single series (one number per week) -- this is an input to Assumptions, not a per-neighborhood metric.
granularity: National single series. Does NOT fit as a Growth Score MetricDef -- per backend/CLAUDE.md every metric must become a percentile within a comparison set, and a national constant is identical for every neighborhood, so it can't be ranked. This is purely a feed for `Assumptions.interest_rate`'s default (or a future `FactorDef.market_estimate()` in app/valuation/), not a neighborhood_metrics row.
update_frequency: Weekly (Thursdays). Methodology changed 2022-11-17 (now based on lender-submitted loan applications rather than the older phone survey) -- a discontinuity to note if anyone later back-tests against pre-2022 values.
history: Back to 1971-04-02. Far more than enough for any backtest use.
license: Copyrighted by Freddie Mac (Primary Mortgage Market Survey); FRED reprints it 'with permission.' Data provided as-is, no warranty. FRED's own API terms are separate and permissive, but the series content itself carries Freddie Mac's copyright notice and FRED asks users to check each series' notes before republishing. Required: cite Freddie Mac (and FRED as retrieval source) wherever the number is shown, e.g. a footnote on the assumptions panel -- do not present it as the project's own figure.
cost: Free. Requires a FRED API key (self-serve signup, instant approval, no human review) -- same shape as the project's existing census_api_key precedent (census_acs.py). Rate limit: 120 req/min general API, 40 req/min for series-observations endpoint specifically -- trivial for a single weekly value.

correlation.reason_not_computed: Not applicable -- this isn't a Growth Score predictor to correlate against HPI/ZORI growth. Its only use is as a financing-cost input to the investment model's cash-flow math, which isn't what evaluate_series.py is designed to test.

recommendation: Recommend with caveats. This directly fixes a real, named gap (a hardcoded 6.5% guess) with an authoritative, long-history, genuinely free series. It is not a Growth Score candidate and should not be wired through sources.yaml/NeighborhoodMetric at all -- an implementer should instead have it refresh `Assumptions.interest_rate`'s default (e.g. a small settings-backed value refreshed on a schedule, the same no-key-leak pattern as other sources) and must add the Freddie Mac/FRED attribution anywhere the rate is displayed. Flagging the copyright notice explicitly so this isn't waved through as 'just a government number' -- Freddie Mac is the actual rights holder, FRED is just the distributor.
evaluated_by: research-analyst routine (via .claude/skills/research-sources/SKILL.md — .claude/agents/research-analyst.md does not exist in this repo)
